name: danareyes_hc
text: Downtown this morning. The city’s new flood defenses have already failed.

The photograph is real and unedited, but it was not taken in Harlow City this morning. It was taken on September 14, 2019 on Wharf Street in Calder Bay’s Old Harbor district during Storm Odessa, and was published by the Calder Bay Courier. The post attaches a genuine image to a false date and location, which is false context. The image also does not show how Harlow’s new flood defenses perform: Harlow’s own status page and weather record show normal conditions and no rainfall today, so a real test of the defenses would need current evidence from Harlow.

Reverse-check the image: search for its distinctive details (a street sign, a shop name) and find its earliest publication, then compare the original caption, date and place with the claim attached to it.

title: Storm Odessa floods Old Harbor; hundreds evacuated
text:
CALDER BAY — Storm Odessa pushed a surge of seawater into the Old Harbor district on Saturday morning, closing streets and forcing the evacuation of about 400 residents.

Water rose above curb height along Wharf Street shortly after 7 a.m., stranding vehicles outside the Old Harbor Chandlery. Fire crews used rescue boats to reach upper-floor apartments.

"We’ve had flooding before, but nothing like this," said shop owner Carl Reuben. City officials said the harbor barrier, built in 1988, was overtopped for roughly two hours.

Public works crews expect to reopen Wharf Street by Monday. Residents can find shelter information at the Calder Bay Civic Hall.

title: Council split over $212M floodgate cost overruns
text:
The Harlow City Council voted 5–4 on Tuesday to approve an additional $19 million for the Harbor Floodgate and Seawall Project, bringing its total cost to $212 million.

Critics argued the project has run over budget twice. "Residents deserve a clear accounting," said Councilmember Ruth Adeyemi. Supporters pointed to engineering reviews that rated the design for a 100-year storm.

Phase 2 of the seawall entered service on Oct. 3. The floodgate has not yet faced a major storm surge.

title: Creek overflow floods Elm Street after record rain
text:
Heavy rain sent Harlow Creek over its banks Monday afternoon, leaving several inches of water on Elm Street for about three hours.

No injuries were reported. The city said it will review drainage along the creek corridor.

name: Satire
text: Nothing in the post or the replies reads as a joke, and the account isn’t a parody outlet. Ask whether it is meant to be taken literally, then look at what else is off.

name: False connection
text: The caption and the picture are about the same thing (flooding). Think about a mismatch that isn’t between caption and image, but between the image and the situation it claims to show.

name: Misleading content
text: Misleading content usually bends real information through framing, cropping or selective detail. Here, consider whether the photo is being used in the setting where it was taken.

name: Imposter content
text: The account has its own history, bio and followers, and isn’t posing as a news outlet or official source. Look at the content rather than who is posting.

name: Manipulated content
text: Compare the post’s photo with any original you can find. If it is the same unedited picture, the problem lies in how it is presented, not in its pixels.

name: Fabricated content
text: The photograph is a real image published elsewhere, so the content itself isn’t invented. Ask where and when it was first published.

name: No information disorder identified
text: Something doesn’t line up. The post makes a claim about this morning, so check whether the evidence actually matches that time and place.
